newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania vows to crack down on pyramid schemes.
newsitem.headline: Albania vows to crack down on pyramid schemes.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha on Saturday vowed to crack down on pyramid investment schemes but warned the opposition against exploiting anger among investors to try to destabilise the ex-communist state.
Albania has been shaken by a series of protests this week by investors furious over the collapse of several of the investment schemes into which many had poured their life savings.
Opposition parties have called for a peaceful demonstration on Sunday against the government, alleging that the ruling Democratic Party had allowed the schemes to proliferate.

Berisha said his conservative government had respected the citizens' democratic right to give and take money on credit but had in no case allowed state institutions to get involved as has happened in other ex-communist states.

"But we...are determined to crack down on every pyramid scheme, every cheating of the citizen, and are determined to establish all the necessary rules and laws to prevent them," Berisha told a party meeting.
The government on Thursday ordered the seizure of some 25.5 billion leks ($255 million) deposited by investment schemes in the country's commercial banks.

Three dubious investment groups have collapsed in the past few weeks in Albania, Europe's poorest country. Infuriated investors clashed with baton-wielding police on Wednesday in a demonstration over the investment projects.

Pyramid schemes boomed in the Balkan nation after the fall of communism in 1990, luring thousands of Albanians into selling homes, land and livestock with promises of big returns on small sums invested.
Berisha accused the mainly leftist opposition of trying to make political capital out of the schemes' collapse.

"I want to make clear to these gentlemen and all others who try to build their success on the misfortune of others...that they have totally failed and that this attempt will have the same luck as previous attempts," he said.

Three opposition parties -- the Socialists, centre-right Democratic Alliance and centre-left Social Democrats -- called a demonstration beginning at 11 a.m. (1000 GMT) in Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square.
"The solution to the political and institutional crisis and economic collapse can only be brought about by fresh elections," the main opposition Socialist Party said.
Berisha said a committee set up to investigate the alleged pyramid schemes would report soon on its findings.

"If the activity (of get-rich-quick schemes) is proved to be a pyramid or a swindle then the frozen deposits and the other property would be returned to the citizens with every cent of interest," he said.
